summary:
Two items in one file: the measured close of the install-snapshot question, and a fresh A1 reading of the pipelined replication cursor (valid:true).

1. The mode-scoped probe executed and both comparisons are decided (receipt 60a9c1c1920e4c7d9cd3b6c031613b69, exit 0). Index 5 recovery_mode_entered records the isolated follower first showing the install signature (applied 87, snapshot 87, log store last 27); index 10 recovered_node_probe_end reports install_signature_seen true, install_signature_ticks 1223, snapshot index 257 above log store last index 197, applied_at_end 257 equal to max_applied_seen and decrease_count 0 — comparison 0 holds with the recovery_mode admission at index 5. Indices 8 and 11 steady_mode_confirmed with 9 and 12 steady_node_probe_end cover the other two nodes (snapshot 257, log 257, applied 257, no decrease) — comparison 1 holds. So no delivered snapshot moved a receiver's applied index backwards: the protection held in the driven scenario, consistent with the recorded source behaviours (term-only check on the receiver; sender-side clamp towards the follower's snapshot-aware reported last index, so delivered requests carried the leader's current snapshot index, not an older one). The investigation is now explained, no defect is claimed, and the boundary is kept explicit: the probe never constructs a leader whose latest snapshot index is below a follower's applied index, so general unreachability is not established. The two earlier probe executions are retained as operands-only corroboration, with the two admission-wiring defects that made their comparisons unknown documented in the limitations. A fact was promoted covering all three executions.

2. New A1 reading of pipelined replication: two cursors stay separate — pipelineSend advances a private send cursor to last pipelined entry index + 1 only after the pipeline accepts the request (replication.go:512-532), while the per-follower nextIndex and the commitment map advance solely from successful decoded responses via updateLastAppended (replication.go:534-567, 655-665). The decoder aborts on the first unsuccessful response, on a newer term (notifyAll(false) plus step-down) and on setup errors such as a compacted prefix, after which the caller falls back to standard replication or to the snapshot path (replication.go:446-510); setPreviousLog additionally handles nextIndex-1 equal to the last snapshot index (replication.go:587-612). Recorded as a behaviour plus an explained, source-only account with no defect claim; limits note that the transport's in-order response contract was assumed and that stop/removal paths in flight were not traced.
